flawed_step: The claim assumes every partition that no single move can improve is a maximum cut. A partition can be locally optimal without being globally optimal.
counterexample: Take G = C4 with vertices 1,2,3,4 and edges 12,23,34,41. The partition {1,2}|{3,4} cuts edges 23 and 41, so its value is 2. Moving 1 gives {2}|{1,3,4} with cut {12,23}, value 2. Moving 2 gives cut {12,41}, value 2. Moving 3 gives {1,2,3}|{4} with cut {34,41}, value 2. Moving 4 gives cut {23,34}, value 2. No move strictly improves the cut, but {1,3}|{2,4} cuts all 4 edges, so the maximum cut is 4 > 2.
assessment_summary: In C4, the partition into two adjacent pairs has cut value 2. All four single-vertex moves also give 2, so no move improves it. The bipartition {1,3}|{2,4} reaches 4, so a locally optimal partition need not be a maximum cut. The statement is false.
